ideaData.title: Split the pack into two 400 V halves for charging instead of fitting a DC booster
ideaData.sourcePointer: BMW_iX3_Gen6_Battery_Benchmark.xlsx › '5 VAVE from this study' row 4
ideaData.technicalDescription: How it works · benchmark (as stated): Two contactor groups reconfigure the pack series/parallel on a 400 V charger; deletes the 400→800 V booster carried elsewhere in the vehicle. Benchmark: BMW Gen6 (illustrative). Spec: +1 contactor set (~€60–90*) in the pack; −1 booster (~€250–400*) at vehicle level
ideaData.costReductionMechanism: Cost effect on the 105 kWh GROSS reference pack (study): +€75 / +€0.7 per kWh GROSS in the pack; −€250 to −€400 at VEHICLE level
ideaData.riskNotes: Certification: RE-TEST — switching contactors are PROTECTED ratings (LV 123, ISO 6469-1). Trade-off: pack-level cost RISES; judge at vehicle level only. Proven. Evidence: tab 2 'Configuration'.

E2 and S2 are cost TRANSFERS that raise pack cost and lower vehicle cost; never book them as pack savings.

ideaData.volumeBasis: No volume stated in the benchmark. Savings across ideas are NOT additive: the study states that ideas in a conflict set are mutually exclusive and that its combined capture is not the sum of the cards.
ideaData.reviewOpenPoints: [MINOR · quality] The vehicle-level figure is gross (booster deleted, −€250 to −€400). S2 states its vehicle-level figure net of the pack adder. Net for E2 would be −€175 to −€325. Evidence: E2: '+€75 ... in the pack; −€250 to −€400 at VEHICLE level'; S2: '+€35 ... in pack; net −€115 to −€265 at VEHICLE level' Recommendation: State E2 as net −€175 to −€325 at vehicle level, so it is consistent with S2. ¶ [MINOR · benchmark] Benchmark claim not found. 'BMW Gen6 splits the pack into two 400 V halves for 400 V charging, no booster': BMW states only that 400 V DC charging remains possible. The mechanism (pack split vs booster) was not found in public sources. The study's own tech tab rates it Tier B 'decoded from technical threads'. Evidence: https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/belux/article/attachment/T0450688FR/632948 (fact sheet: '800V ... charging at 400V DC points will, of course, still be possible'); no source found for split Recommendation: Keep the '(illustrative)' tag. Do not present the mechanism as confirmed.
